([[Omaha, Nebraska]]) | college = *[[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] (2019–2023) *[[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] (2023–2024) *[[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] (2024–2025) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025]]) * First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) }} '''John Tonje''' ({{IPAc-en|t|ɑː|n|ˈ|dʒ|eɪ}} {{Respell|tahn|JAY}}; born April 23, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]], and [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]]. ==High school career== Tonje attended [[Omaha Central High School]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]], where he played basketball. As a sophomore, Tonje averaged 1.6 points per game but improved to 13.6 points per games as a junior. He was the second leading scorer for the Omaha Central Eagles during his junior campaign and connected on 46 percent of his three point attempts. As a senior, Tonje averaged a Nebraska Class A State best 23.8 points along with 6.1 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.4 assists per game. He led the Eagles to a 22-6 record and a runner-up finish at the state tournament. His 73 triples and 82 percent free throw percentage were tops at Class A. He set his school's single-season scoring record as a senior and earned first-team All-State by USA Today and All-Class State All-Tournament team honors.{{cite web|url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/john-tonje/13195|title=John Tonje Wisconsin Bio|website=uwbadgers.com|date=November 16, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} for the Rams during his freshman and sophomore seasons.{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/5-takeaways-david-roddy-stars-in-a-resilient-comeback-effort-from-colorado-state-in-the-paradise-jam/|title=5 career high 31 points in the first game of his junior season against [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]].{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/john-tonje-dischon-thomas-stand-out-in-a-dominant-team-performance-by-the-rams/|title=John Tonje, Dischon Thomas stand out in a dominant team performance by the Rams|website=thednrv.com|date=November 10, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje was a key to the success being dubbed the [[Sixth man]] that helped lead the Rams to a [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] and getting to the semifinals.{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/year-in-review-john-tonje-shined-as-colorado-states-sixth-man/|title=Year-in-review: John Tonje shined as Colorado State's sixth man|website=tdnvr.com|date=April 12, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje bounced back and forth between the bench and starting lineup throughout his junior season. He was a big part of the success of the [[2020–21 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team]] that had a program best 16-1 start to the season.{{cite web|url=https://csurams.com/news/2022/1/22/mens-basketball-csu-runs-record-to-program-best-15-1-with-73-53-win-at-air-force|title=CSU Runs Record to Program Best 15-1 With 73-53 Win At Air Force|website=csurams.com|date=January 22, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje and the Rams qualified for the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as an at-large bid for the program's first time since 2013 finishing the season with a 25-6 record. The sixth seeded Rams were upset by the 11th seeded [[2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]].{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2022/03/17/michigan-tops-colorado-state-to-begin-march-madness-2022/|title=Michigan storms back to top Colorado State as March Madness 2022 begins|website=nypost.com|date=March 17, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje became a full-time starter for the first time during his senior season. He posted career per game highs in points (14.6), rebounds (4.7), assists (1.3), steals (0.8) and blocks (0.3). Tonje decided to enter the [[transfer portal]] after his 4th season due to the extra year of eligibility from to the [[COVID-19]] season rule.{{cite web|url=https://milehighsports.com/csu-basketball-updates-john-tonje-enters-transfer-portal-mckenna-hofschild-will-be-back/|title=CSU Basketball updates: John Tonje enters transfer portal, McKenna Hofschild will be back|website=nypost.com|date=March 22, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2024}} ===Missouri=== Tonje decided to transfer to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite web|url=https://missouri.rivals.com/news/summer-sessions-john-tonje|title=Summer Sessions: John Tonje|website=missouri.rivals.com|date=July 24, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje only appeared in eight games with the Tigers due to a season-ending foot injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/missouri/basketball/mizzou-guard-john-tonje-to-miss-remainder-of-season|title=Mizzou Guard John Tonje to Miss Remainder of Season|website=si.com|date=July 16, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje was granted a medical redshirt and a sixth year of eligibility. He then decided to enter the transfer portal for a second time.{{cite web|url=https://www.rockmnation.com/2024/4/15/24131262/report-john-tonje-set-to-enter-the-transfer-portal|title=REPORT: John Tonje set to enter the transfer portal|website=rockmnation.com|date=April 15, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} ===Wisconsin=== Tonje was ranked as the 296th transfer portal player following the 2023-24 season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/longformarticle/taking-stock-of-15-transfer-portal-ranking-misses-from-2024-aj-storr-johnell-davis-kobe-johnson-kanaan-carlyle-jonas-aidoo-aidan-mahaney-pj-haggerty--245264963/#2595027|title=Taking stock of 15 transfer portal ranking misses from the 2024 cycle|website=247sports.com|date=February 6, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} Tonje originally committed to [[Richard Pitino]] and [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]].{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/college/new-mexico-lobos/news/missouri-transfer-guard-john-tonje-commits-to-new-mexico/|title=Missouri transfer guard John Tonje commits to New Mexico|website=on3.com|date=April 25, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Less than a week later, Tonje decommitted from New Mexico and committed to Wisconsin.{{cite web|url=https://badgerswire.usatoday.com/2024/05/02/wisconsin-badgers-transfer-portal-commitment-john-tonje/|title=Wisconsin lands commitment from Missouri transfer guard John Tonje|website=baderswire.usatoday.com|date=May 2, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} In only his fourth career game with the Badgers, Tonje scored a career high 41 points in an upset victory over the 9th ranked [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona Wildcats]]. His 41 points were the fourth most in a single game in Badgers history. Tonje also broke the Wisconsin single game record for made free throws with 21.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/wisconsin-badgers-tonje-arizona-75307c6292b440692db1e8474caaa47e|title=Wisconsin guard John Tonje is wasting no time making his mark at his new |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/4593043/john-tonje |access-date=November 16, 2024 |website=ESPN}} ==Personal life== Tonje is the son of Sara and Jean. His father, Jean "Bertin" Tonje, is a native of [[Cameroon]] and played soccer for the [[Cameroon national football team]]. He has two brothers, Malcolm and Texan. He earned his bachelor’s degree from Colorado State in Business/Real Estate and is currently studying Sports Leadership as a graduate student. {{cite web|url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/john-tonje/13195|title=2024–25 Men's Basketball Roster John Tonje|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He frequently mentions his faith on social media. He has said, “Sometimes it’s hard to believe. Last night, I was reading an article about being All-American, which, I mean, doesn’t even look right.
